rationale: The blind lens failed to produce a parseable file after two waits, so this round has no context-free human-judgment pass and confidence is capped at low. Two critical defects block: CR-001 the standard/V2 deselection check wrongly suppresses the independently-selected V2 tool variant (acceptance AC9 fail, spec-independence fail); CR-002 the migration adds deselected_default_tools with no backfill, so every pre-existing assistant loads it as None, crashing chat-time tool assembly and silently bypassing the direct-invoke deselection gate. 1 deferred (KB toolkit visibility tied to pre-existing ES-configured gating, out of this change's scope) and 1 dismissed as noise (unnormalized duplicate entries in deselected_default_tools, cosmetic, no documented standard makes it blocking). Standards audit is clean with no coverage gap.

findings.title: V2 tool variant wrongly suppressed by deselection
findings.problem: _add_code_tools ANDs `REPO_TREE_TOOL.name not in assistant.deselected_default_tools` (and the equivalent for CODE_SEARCH_TOOL) into the same condition that gates the V2 'with filtering' variant, so deselecting the standard tool name also suppresses the V2 variant even when it was independently selected via toolkits.
findings.impact: Violates spec D1/AC9: selecting a V2 variant alongside deselecting its standard name must leave the V2 variant unaffected ('V2 still wins'). The shipped test test_add_code_tools_skips_repo_tree_when_deselected encodes the wrong behavior as expected, so CI will not catch a regression here.
findings.recommendation: Split the condition: gate only the standard (with_filtering=False) call on '... not in deselected_default_tools'; keep the V2-filtered call (repo_tree_with_filtering/code_search_with_filtering True) unconditional on deselection, per AC9. Update test_add_code_tools_skips_repo_tree_when_deselected accordingly.

findings.title: Missing backfill crashes/bypasses deselection for legacy assistants
findings.problem: The migration adds deselected_default_tools as nullable JSON with no server_default and no data backfill on either table. Every assistant/assistant_configuration row created before this migration loads with the attribute as None, because SQLModel's default_factory=list only applies to new Python-constructed instances, not to values loaded from an existing NULL column.
findings.impact: toolkit_service.py's _add_kb_tools/_add_code_tools (lines 1484, 1605, 1616) do 'X.name in assistant.deselected_default_tools' with no None-guard, so the next chat turn for any pre-existing assistant with a CODE or KNOWLEDGE_BASE context raises TypeError and breaks tool assembly entirely. Conversely, tool_execution_service.py's direct-invoke gate (lines 319-326) explicitly treats a non-list value as 'nothing deselected' and silently skips enforcement, making the deselection security gate a no-op for the same legacy assistants. assistant_version_service.py:127 and assistant_version_migration_service.py (lines 80, 116, 145) also propagate this None into AssistantConfiguration(deselected_default_tools=...), a list[str]-typed (non-Optional) field, likely failing validation and breaking version creation/rollback/migration.
findings.recommendation: Backfill existing rows in the migration (e.g. op.execute("UPDATE assistants SET deselected_default_tools = '[]' WHERE deselected_default_tools IS NULL") and the same for assistant_configurations, or add server_default='[]' then drop it) so no row can load as None; as defense in depth also guard every consumer with (assistant.deselected_default_tools or []).
